reasoning: The two sets share most of their structure: the same 10 milestones, the same 46 M1 tasks, the same pipelines, and the same reference handling (the PCA reference is assigned to the qrisk study milestone, and the TFT files go to M8). B fixes several real problems that A still has. First, A replaced the WebSocket progress channel the user asked for with Server-Sent Events. AD-07 even lists WebSockets as a rejected alternative. B uses a WebSocket throughout: the architecture, contracts, pipelines, plan and packets. Second, A uses yfinance for the cross-check, but the user specified yahooquery. B switches AD-03, PB-03 and the stack to yahooquery and keeps the chart endpoint as a fallback. Third, A gives exit criteria only to M1, while B gives every milestone checkable exit criteria. Fourth, B adds closed-form golden cases for the point-in-time core (split and dividend returns, add-date membership, a late dividend invisible as of K−1, a reused ticker, first-known stamping), where A's qdata has no golden cases even though its checkpoint says "All golden cases pass". B's packets are also more complete. For example, A's M1-T21 mount_reads packet leaves out query.Company, Actions, Returns, checks.Failure and xcheck.Comparison, and has no Catalog input, even though CompanyPage carries failures; B adds all of these. B also cleans up the plan: M1-T04 no longer claims DATA-01, which the plan defers; it removes A's create_app check, which needed a route list that doesn't exist yet; it handles the deferred mount_studies explicitly in the PL-10 wiring task; and it moves the backtest cost cases into M8, which runs the backtest with costs. Neither set is perfect. Both still use nasdaq-data-link rather than Sharadar's own API, and B's probes still list yfinance docs it read. Even so, B is clearly stronger.
